title: SCOPE: piloting a capacity-aware roadmap prioritization rubric
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: We will pilot a new prioritization rubric called SCOPE (Scalability, Customer impact, Operational cost, Performance impact, Effort) to make roadmap trade-offs explicit for initiatives that materially affect inference economics and latency. Motivation: existing RICE-like signals emphasize reach and effort but lack a standard way to fold in capacity sensitivity (GPU pool saturation), per-token cost deltas, and latency SLO risk. SCOPE is intended to sit alongside OKR mapping and capacity forecasts so PMs can compare features, infra work, and model upgrades on a single scale.

How SCOPE works (high level): For each candidate initiative, PMs score five dimensions 0-5: 1) Scalability: expected change to steady-state resource demand (0 none -> 5 multiplies GPU requirement x10), 2) Customer impact: measurable user/business value (0 none -> 5 strategic imperative), 3) Operational cost delta: expected change in $/M tokens served (0 decrease -> 5 large increase), 4) Performance impact: expected effect on latency SLOs (0 improves -> 5 high regression risk), 5) Effort: estimated implementation points (0 tiny -> 5 major). Each dimension has a weight; default weighting: Scalability 25%, Customer impact 30%, Operational cost 20%, Performance impact 15%, Effort -10% (negative weight so higher effort reduces priority). The composite SCOPE score is normalized to 0-100. Thresholds: >70 green (high priority), 45-70 consider with trade-offs, <45 low.

Integration points: - OKRs: map Customer impact to OKR confidence bands and tag initiatives that unlock >=1 OKR key result. - Capacity planning: use Dedicated capacity forecast (ENG-provided) to convert Scalability into weeks of required reserve capacity. - Console observability: connect to cost-by-route dashboard to auto-populate Operational cost estimates where available. - Rollouts: tie Performance impact to canary SLOs and release gating.

Pilot plan: Apply SCOPE to 3 initiatives planned for next cycle: (A) streaming batching improvements, (B) dedicated KV-cache persistence work, (C) conversational model swap for mid-sized customers. For each, we will run blinded scoring by 3 PMs, 1 design lead, and 2 engineers, reconcile differences in a calibration session, and publish final scores into the roadmap deck.

Measurement of success: - Adoption: at least 6 PMs and 2 platform leads use SCOPE for prioritization decisions in the pilot quarter. - Predictive validity: SCOPE ranking correlates with realized cost delta and latency regressions at Pearson r >= 0.4 across pilot initiatives. - Cycle velocity: average planning time per initiative reduces by 20% (faster decisions).

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: noisy cost estimates. Mitigation: use conservative bands and require data-engineering hookup for any score >3 on Operational cost. - Risk: double-counting customer value across metrics. Mitigation: calibration guide with examples and a mandatory OKR link if Customer impact >=4.

Next steps: 1) Publish SCOPE rubric doc and examples (confluence). 2) Build a one-page SCOPE scorecard template in the console (design + eng effort). 3) Run the pilot with 3 initiatives and present results at the roadmap review on 2026-04-05.
